rows.claim: defendant A: mirroring the 2x3 board left-right and renaming the slide directions with it ('a tile slides left' becomes 'a tile slides right', up/down unchanged) preserves the puzzle exactly -- directions are bound to board coordinates, so the true symmetry carries its own direction renaming; declared under the explicit caliber with per-element action maps

defendant B: the same left-right mirror with the directions PINNED (a slide left must stay a slide left) -- the naive-intuition claim that 'the board looks the same mirrored', filed deliberately under the fixed caliber to show it is the direction renaming, not the state permutation, that makes defendant A true

positive control: padding states 720 and 1023 have the same behavior shape (every action a single self-loop, reward 0), so the swap is a genuine symmetry under the pinned-direction reading and should be admitted everywhere

main positive control: the FULL 4-element rectangle symmetry group V4 = C2 x C2 (identity, left-right mirror, top-bottom mirror, 180-degree rotation), each element carrying its own direction renaming -- the third non-trivial positive control of this court, after mini2048's D4 and lightsout3's D4, and a third group structure (the board is a non-square rectangle: no 90-degree rotation exists, machine-verified by enumerating all 720 cell bijections against the adjacency graph)
